problem: Prior equivariant differentiable planners (SymVIN) only work on discrete 2D grids with discrete D4 symmetry and need exactly 4 cameras matching the group, limiting their use for real robot navigation in unstructured continuous space.
motivation: Learning-based navigation needs lots of data and gives no generalization guarantees. Navigation has inherent Euclidean E(2) symmetry from reference-frame changes, which allows parameter sharing and better data efficiency, stability and generalization. Exploiting it on irregular geometric graphs and with multi-camera input requires new layers.
key_idea: Formulate navigation as value iteration on a 2D geometric graph implemented with E(2)-equivariant (steerable) message passing, plus a learnable lifting layer that maps a C_K camera array's features to a larger rotation group.
insight: Equivariance mainly improves data efficiency, learning-curve smoothness and size generalization rather than always peak accuracy. On Graph World, R2 x D8 gets 72.17/61.90 vs 63.10/54.76 for No-Sym, and trained on 100 samples it beats non-symmetric baselines trained on 512. Group ablation shows D8 > D4 >> C8 on 27x27 (84.52 / 82.11 / 40.51), suggesting the group should match the environment's symmetries (mazes have reflection symmetry). On regular grids the grid-specialized SymVIN still wins.
method: Geometric graph formulation: nodes are states with 2D position and features (goal, obstacle, image features); edges are transitions; the planner outputs a continuous relative movement in R^2 per node
MP-VIN: value iteration as K rounds of message passing computing Q and V (max over channel); the final Q gives the action map
Translation equivariance: messages use only relative positions x_i - x_j
Rotation/reflection equivariance: propagate and update MLPs are steerable G-equivariant (e2cnn, G=D8 or C4) satisfying the kernel constraint; Theorem 1 proves the Bellman operator is E(2)-equivariant

Equivariant lift layer: maps images from a C_K camera array (e.g. 4 cameras) to features on a larger group (e.g. D8/SO(2)); enforces equivariance only for the subgroup C_K via a restricted representation, so later layers can be G-equivariant
Mapper network: for unknown maps, a CNN image encoder plus a grid/graph decoder estimates an occupancy grid/graph from 4-view RGB, trained jointly with the planner

setting.backbone: MP-VIN equivariant message-passing planner (trained from scratch); ResNet-34 features (last layer trained) for the Habitat experiment
setting.training_data: Synthetic mazes and random graphs with Dijkstra labels (10K/2K/2K train/val/test for Grid World, 1K/200/200 for others); Miniworld renders; HM3DSem refrigerator graphs (20 random 128-node graphs per scene)
setting.observation: Fully observable map or graph with goal; 4-direction egocentric RGB (32x32, 128x128 in Habitat) per node; assumes accurate localization
setting.action_space: continuous relative 2D displacement on graph nodes (discretized to NEWS for grid baselines)
setting.privileged: Fully observable environment: observations at all nodes given at once; GT object location used only for training labels; accurate localization assumed

numbers.evidence: Table I, averaged test success rate, Grid World 15x15
Table II, Performance in semantic navigation task

numbers_note: Benchmarks are the paper's own synthetic tasks, not standard benchmarks. Learning curves and data-efficiency/size-generalization results are given only in figures. Appendix ablation Table: C8 91.10/40.51, D4 90.59/82.11, D8 91.50/84.52 on Grid World 15/27.
results: MP-VIN with R2 ⋊ D8 has the best success on Graph World (72.17/61.90 vs SymVIN 24.40/27.53, VIN 18.75/20.09) and Miniworld-Graph (96.96 vs SymVIN 27.98). It has smoother learning curves and better size generalization. On regular grids SymVIN remains better (Grid World 95.85/93.73 vs 91.50/84.52). In Habitat, C4 symmetry adds 4.57 points SR (74.27 vs 69.70).
limitations: Assumes a fully observable state: observations of all nodes are given at once, as in VIN, and perfect localization, which is impractical for real robots
Only proof-of-concept semantic navigation (one object class, no real robot, no partial observability)
Loses to the grid-specialized SymVIN on regular grid mazes, and results have high variance in some settings
builds_on: Geometric message passing (EGNN, Brandstetter et al.)
